title: China's Slowest City Was Born as a 1718 Army Camp — Chengdu | China Travel Expert
description:
Follow me into Chengdu — the big city that turned an old army garrison into China's slowest, most relaxed street.

Chengdu's famous Kuanzhai Alleys (Wide, Narrow and Well lanes) began in 1718 as a Qing-dynasty Manchu garrison city, built to house Eight-Banner troops and their families. Three centuries later that grid is teahouses, courtyards and slow afternoons. Chengdu is defined by its 10,000-plus teahouses and the local 'bashi' (巴适 — just right) way of life; the lidded gaiwan tea set itself was invented here, and afternoons mean jasmine tea, mahjong and ear-cleaning.

🧭 Expert Tip: Skip the crowded Kuanzhai main lane at midday. Go on a weekday morning, then walk to the century-old Heming Teahouse in People's Park for open-air gaiwan tea under the plane trees — the authentic, un-touristy version of the same slow-city culture.

成都最慢的巷子，三百年前竟是清朝军营。
